transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-03-18
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Simmons, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair, Samir Khan (Oakridge)

Auto Summary:
Redwood and Oakridge scoped a 4-week POC focused on model quality for clinical note summarization and triage assistance. Customer will provide de-identified prompts, Redwood will run benchmarks and deliver a quality eval report. Key knobs: hallucination rates, structured format adherence (FHIR-ish), latency SLOs, and cost per inference.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, quick round of intros?
[00:12] Laura Simmons: yeah hi i'm laura, head of ai at oakridge, focusing on clinical nlp and the downstream triage workflows, excited to scope this poc.
[00:22] Diego Alvarez: diego here, director of eng, i'll own integration and our staging dataset.
[00:28] Priya Nair: priya, security, i'll be the compliance contact — HIPAA, BAAs, that sort of thing.
[00:35] Maya Chen: awesome. ravi, do you want to kick into the proposed quality eval plan?
[00:40] Ravi Patel: sure. so high-level our goal is to validate model quality for two primary tasks: 1) chart-note summarization to a structured summary, and 2) triage label / urgency scoring from notes. we'll use a mixed automated + human scoring approach.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: for the POC duration we're proposing 4 weeks: week 0 is setup/integration, week 1 baseline runs, week 2 tuning (quantization/profile, batching), week 3 expanded validation and human review, week 4 final report and handoff.
[01:30] Diego Alvarez: that timeline looks reasonable, what's the workload size you recommend for meaningful results?
[01:38] Ravi Patel: for quality you'd want at minimum ~500 golden prompts with gold outputs (these are canonical examples we expect the model to get right) and ~2,000 random production prompts for stress/regression. for human review we'll sample ~200 outputs across different buckets.
[02:05] Laura Simmons: 500 golden prompts — what do you mean by golden? like exact phrasing and expected structured fields?
[02:12] Ravi Patel: correct, golden prompts are example inputs + vetted ground-truth outputs. they should cover core entities, formatting edge cases, and clinically sensitive scenarios. they help check regressions and are used for automated scoring (exact match / field-level F1).
[02:35] Maya Chen: important to note oakridge wants format adherence for FHIR-ish summaries — that will be part of the format checks.
[02:42] Priya Nair: and also no PHI in any shared data; we'll de-identify before transfer. we'll need a BAA and SOC2 docs before any private deployment.
[02:55] Maya Chen: noted, we'll share our compliance pack and scope of the BAA.
[03:00] Ravi Patel: on benchmarks — metrics we'll capture: field-level F1 for structured outputs, Exact Match for critical fields (meds, allergies), hallucination rate (percentage of outputs containing fabricated entities), BLEU/ROUGE for free-text where appropriate, latency percentiles (p50/p95) for 256 & 512 token contexts, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: hallucination checks will be both automated heuristics (e.g., named entity cross-check against input and KB) and manual spot-checks flagged by discrepancy rules. format checks will assert required fields and JSON validity for structured outputs.
[03:50] Samir Khan: can you give a concrete acceptance criteria example?
[03:55] Ravi Patel: sure, example acceptance thresholds for the POC: field-level F1 >= 0.88, critical-field exact match >= 0.92, hallucination rate < 3% on the eval set, p95 latency < 400ms for 256-token requests on dedicated pool, and cost < $0.08 per 1k tokens (hosted baseline). these are starting points to agree on.
[04:25] Laura Simmons: those numbers seem in the ballpark; we'll validate internally but we might require stricter exact match on allergies.
[04:34] Maya Chen: we can make the thresholds configurable per-field, that's typical.
[04:38] Diego Alvarez: what's your scoring approach for combining automated metrics and human review? do you give weight to human labels?
[04:45] Ravi Patel: we propose a composite score: 70% automated metrics (weighted combination: 40% field F1, 20% exact match on critical fields, 10% hallucination penalty), 30% human evaluation (scale 1-5 averaged and normalized). final pass/fail requires meeting automated thresholds and human average >= 4.0.
[05:10] Priya Nair: for human review, who conducts it? we prefer Oakridge snr clinicians to validate sensitive cases — but Redwood can provide annotation guidelines and optionally run the initial human review.
[05:24] Maya Chen: happy to provide the rubric and a sample of annotated reviews. we can also run the bulk automated scoring and surface a review queue for your clinicians.
[05:33] Samir Khan: what about regression testing — you mentioned a regression suite?
[05:37] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll maintain a regression suite that includes the 500 golden prompts and edge-case tests. before any model change we re-run the suite and report any drop in the composite score. we'll also capture diffs of outputs for quick triage.
[05:55] Diego Alvarez: do you support pinned model versions and automatic fallback in case latency spikes?
[06:00] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood supports model pinning and routing policies. for the POC we can set up a canary + fallback to a smaller model if needed. that will also feed into cost controls.
[06:12] Ravi Patel: on workload sizing and throughput — what's your expected concurrency and QPS for the POC runs?
[06:20] Diego Alvarez: for benchmarks we plan batch runs at ~50 concurrent requests for throughput testing, and a 10 QPS steady-state for latency SLO validation. peak for a short window might be 150 concurrent.
[06:35] Ravi Patel: ok we'll provision a dedicated pool for the POC and run both steady-state and burst tests. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and token throughput.
[06:44] Laura Simmons: regarding hallucinations: do you have a standard way to detect fabricated medical facts? that's critical for us.
[06:51] Ravi Patel: we use NER/KB cross-check heuristics to flag entities not present in the input or linked sources. for more robust detection we can run an entailment model comparing output statements to the source; items with low entailment score get flagged for human review.
[07:08] Priya Nair: for private deployment options, we need KMS integration, customer-managed keys, and audit logs to feed into our SIEM. can Redwood support that in the POC?
[07:18] Maya Chen: yes, we have a Private deployment option that supports customer KMS and audit log forwarding. for the POC we'll run hosted for speed, and a private variant for a subset of runs to validate the compliance stack.
[07:32] Diego Alvarez: any constraints on sample size for human review? we said ~200, is that per iteration?
[07:38] Ravi Patel: typically 200 sampled across buckets (critical fields, edge cases, standard cases) is enough for signal in a POC. we can increase if you want more statistical power.
[07:50] Samir Khan: how do we share the golden prompts securely? S3 presigned URLs?
[07:54] Priya Nair: presigned S3 is fine but must be in our VPC or use customer-managed encryption. we'll provide access details after the BAA.
[08:03] Maya Chen: noted — we'll accept an S3 location or secure upload.
[08:07] Ravi Patel: examples of golden prompts:
- "Note: Patient reports chest pain radiating to left arm. Current meds: aspirin 81mg daily. Summarize in structured JSON with fields: summary, problems, meds, allergies."
- "Note: 67yo female, hx dm, mentions penicillin allergy. Extract meds and allergies and output in FHIR-like JSON."
These will have gold outputs from your clinical team.
[08:40] Laura Simmons: we'll prepare that set and include tricky edge cases like conflicting medication mentions and negation.
[08:48] Ravi Patel: on regression tests, we'll also include failure-mode tests — e.g., hallucination triggers where the model historically invents lab values; those should be flagged if present.
[08:58] Diego Alvarez: curious about model variants and quantization: will you test quantized weights for cost/lateny?
[09:05] Ravi Patel: yes, part of week 2 tuning we'll test quantized variants that reduce GPU memory and typically lower cost, and we'll evaluate quality delta on the golden set. we'll report tradeoffs.
[09:18] Maya Chen: anything else from Oakridge on acceptance criteria?
[09:22] Laura Simmons: we want a clear regression policy — if a model update during the POC reduces composite score by >2 points, we consider the previous model the baseline.
[09:32] Samir Khan: and we need exportable artifacts: CSV of metric results, diffs, and a short report.
[09:38] Ravi Patel: we'll provide a final report + dashboard access and raw result artifacts.
[09:44] Priya Nair: legal will want to see the data retention policy for the hosted runs.
[09:48] Maya Chen: we'll include retention settings and we can disable retention for PII-sensitive datasets.
[09:53] Diego Alvarez: okay last question: do you run adversarial tests for prompt injection or model jailbreaks?
[09:59] Ravi Patel: we can include a small prompt-injection suite that tries known patterns; we'll measure success rate and include mitigations (response templates, content filters).
[10:10] Maya Chen: great. to recap — Redwood sends SOW + compliance docs, Oakridge provides de-identified golden set and staging access, Redwood provisions POC env and runs baseline + tuning + validation per the 4-week timeline. action items and owners captured in the doc.
[10:30] Laura Simmons: thanks everyone, we'll target dates in the action items.
[10:34] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff.

End of call.

Notes on Scoring Approach (from the call):
- Automated metrics: field-level F1, exact-match on critical fields, hallucination rate, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable.
- Human eval: per-sample 1-5 scale using rubric (accuracy, completeness, format adherence); human weight ~30%.
- Composite score: weighted sum, must meet automated thresholds and human average >=4.0 for acceptance.
- Regression policy: failing regression (>2 point drop) triggers rollback/pinning.

Benchmark Plan Outline (from the call):
- Dataset: 500 golden prompts + gold outputs, 2,000 random production prompts, 200 human-review samples.
- Tests: baseline quality, throughput (50 concurrent), latency SLOs (10 QPS steady), burst tests up to 150 concurrent.
- Checks: format validation (JSON, FHIR field presence), hallucination detection (NER/KB + entailment), prompt-injection suite.
- Deliverables: CSV of per-sample metrics, diffs against golden outputs, dashboard access, final POC report.

POC Timeline (agreed):
- 2026-03-18 to 2026-03-24: setup & transfer of data, SOW signed
- 2026-03-25 to 2026-03-31: baseline runs on hosted environment
- 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-07: tuning (quantization, batching, routing) and private variant validation
- 2026-04-08 to 2026-04-14: expanded validation, human review, final report

Deliverables to expect: POC SOW, compliance pack (SOC2, BAA guidance), benchmark harness + run logs, final quality report with composite scoring and recommended model+config for production.
